item.title: Pakistani military drone strikes kill three civilians in Balochistan
item.description: Three civilians were reportedly killed and two others critically injured in separate drone strikes in Balochistan's Ziarat and Kech districts, according to local sources, as reported by The ...
item.content:encoded:
Pakistani military drone strikes kill three civilians in Balochistan Separate drone strikes in Balochistan's Ziarat and Kech districts reportedly killed three civilians and injured two others. These incidents add to rising civilian casualties from military drone operations in the region, amid ongoing human rights concerns regarding extrajudicial actions and security practices. ANI | Updated: 21-10-2026 17:36 IST | Created: 21-10-2026 17:36 IST

Representative Image (File Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Three civilians were reportedly killed and two others critically injured in separate drone strikes in Balochistan's Ziarat and Kech districts, according to local sources, as reported by The Balochistan Post. According to The Balochistan Post, the first incident occurred in the Anzargi area of Ziarat, where a drone strike killed a shepherd and left two other people seriously wounded. Residents said the shepherd's body remained stranded in the mountainous area, with the local administration yet to initiate efforts to recover his remains. In a separate incident in Kech district, a Pakistani military drone reportedly struck a vehicle in the Dashtuk border area, killing two civilians. Local sources identified the deceased as Shah Jan and Samad Jan. The latest incidents add to a growing number of reported civilian casualties associated with drone and quadcopter operations across Balochistan. The repeated allegations have raised questions about the safety of residents in areas affected by military activity and the measures taken to prevent harm to non-combatants. Earlier this month, two men sustained serious injuries in a suspected drone strike in the Khadkocha area of Mastung district. In another incident in Panjgur, an explosion killed two children and wounded three others. Local sources alleged that the blast was caused by explosives attached to a Pakistani military quadcopter, as highlighted by The Balochistan Post. A previous strike on September 24 in Balicha, Kech district, reportedly killed four young men and injured two others. The victims' families maintained that the men had travelled to the area for a picnic and strongly disputed the authorities' portrayal of them as suspected militants, as reported by The Balochistan Post. Pakistan continues to face serious allegations over enforced disappearances and extrajudicial killings, particularly in regions such as Balochistan and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. Human rights groups, including Amnesty International and Human Rights Watch, have repeatedly raised concerns about missing activists, students and political workers allegedly taken by security agencies without legal process. (ANI)

item.title: Russia releases American citizen Stephen Hubbard after US envoy Witkoff’s visit to St Petersburg
item.description: Russia on Wednesday released American citizen Stephen Hubbard, who had been detained in the country for more than four years, following US special envoy Steve Witkoff’s visit to Saint Petersburg, CNN ...
item.content:encoded:
Russia releases American citizen Stephen Hubbard after US envoy Witkoff’s visit to St Petersburg Russia on Wednesday released American citizen Stephen Hubbard, who had been detained in the country for more than four years, following US special envoy Steve Witkoff’s visit to Saint Petersburg, CNN reported. ANI | Updated: 21-10-2026 16:32 IST | Created: 21-10-2026 16:32 IST

American citizen Stephen Hubbard released from Russian detention (Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

Country:

Russia

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Russia on Wednesday released American citizen Stephen Hubbard, who had been detained in the country for more than four years, following US special envoy Steve Witkoff’s visit to Saint Petersburg, CNN reported. Hubbard, a retired teacher from Michigan, had been designated by the US State Department as wrongfully detained. His release comes after US President Donald Trump said on Tuesday that he had raised the American citizen’s case with Russian President Vladimir Putin, CNN reported. Ahead of Witkoff’s visit, a US official said the envoy’s trip was “expected to include efforts to seek the release of wrongfully detained American citizen Hubbard, reflecting President Trump’s continued commitment to bringing Americans home.” Hubbard spent decades working abroad as an English teacher before moving to the eastern Ukrainian city of Izyum in 2014. The city was occupied by Russian forces at the beginning of Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022. Russian prosecutors alleged that Hubbard had fought alongside Ukrainian forces in Izyum after signing a contract for approximately USD 1,000 per month, according to Russian state media. However, his sister, Patricia Hubbard Fox, rejected the accusation, describing it as a lie. Hubbard’s release marks the latest development in efforts to secure the freedom of Americans detained in Russia, where individual cases have featured prominently in diplomatic engagement between Washington and Moscow. In August, Robert Gilman, a US Marine veteran held in Russian detention, was released on humanitarian grounds amid serious concerns about his health. Gilman was reportedly severely emaciated when he returned to the United States aboard a specialised medical aircraft. The organisation advocating for his release alleged that he had been tortured during his detention. Witkoff’s visit to St Petersburg comes amid continuing diplomatic efforts over the Russia-Ukraine war. According to Al Jazeera, the US special envoy arrived in the Russian city for a scheduled meeting with Putin. Meanwhile, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has called for a swift end to the conflict and urged the United States and European allies to help advance peace efforts. (ANI)

item.title: Trump says data centres should pay local communities "dividends" to win public support
item.description: US President Donald Trump said data centre operators should pay local communities or individuals a “dividend” to secure public support for their projects, while calling for large facilities to ...
item.content:encoded:
Trump says data centres should pay local communities "dividends" to win public support US President Donald Trump said data centre operators should pay local communities or individuals a “dividend” to secure public support for their projects, while calling for large facilities to generate their own electricity and supply surplus power to the local community or grid. ANI | Updated: 21-10-2026 12:03 IST | Created: 21-10-2026 12:03 IST

US President Donald Trump (Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

US President Donald Trump said data centre operators should pay local communities or individuals a “dividend” to secure public support for their projects, while calling for large facilities to generate their own electricity and supply surplus power to the local community or grid. In a post on Truth Social, Trump said he had been closely monitoring data centres and concluded that new and large facilities should be required to generate their own electricity, arguing that this could help prevent increases in local electricity prices and potentially lead to a substantial decrease. “If companies want to make their Data Centers popular, pay the community, and/or individuals within the community, a ‘dividend’,” Trump said in the post. He added that data centres that had been unpopular in certain areas had become popular after companies reached financial agreements with local communities. “I have watched the process closely, and data centers that were highly unpopular in a certain area, have become extremely popular when a financial deal is struck,” he said. Trump also called on companies to negotiate such arrangements with communities to facilitate the construction of data centres, ending his post with the appeal: “Make deals, and get them built!!! great for the U.S.A.” His remarks come as data centres, which support cloud computing and artificial intelligence workloads, require substantial amounts of electricity to operate. His post focused on addressing local concerns over power costs and ensuring that communities hosting such facilities receive financial benefits. Trump said large data centres should return or sell any excess electricity they generate to the local community or power grid. He suggested that the approach could help ease pressure on electricity prices rather than contribute to increases. The proposed community dividend would offer another way for operators to address local opposition, with Trump citing financial agreements as a factor that could change public sentiment towards projects. However, the post did not specify how the proposed electricity-generation requirement or community payments would be implemented, what form the dividends would take, or whether the administration would introduce a formal policy or regulatory mandate. Trump concluded that negotiating financial arrangements with local communities could help companies gain acceptance for data centre projects and accelerate their construction across the United States. (ANI)

item.description: Student protests erupted across Indonesia over rising living costs, economic concerns and forest fires, with demonstrators criticising President Prabowo Subianto's policies on the second anniversary ...
item.content:encoded:
Student protests erupt across Indonesia over rising living costs, forest fires Student protests erupted across Indonesia over rising living costs, economic concerns and forest fires, with demonstrators criticising President Prabowo Subianto's policies on the second anniversary of his administration, The Jakarta Post reported. ANI | Updated: 21-10-2026 09:40 IST | Created: 21-10-2026 09:40 IST

Demonstrators protest against the government's handling of wildfires and demand an end to corruption, collusion and nepotism, in Jakarta (Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Student protests erupted across Indonesia over rising living costs, economic concerns and forest fires, with demonstrators criticising President Prabowo Subianto's policies on the second anniversary of his administration, The Jakarta Post reported. Demonstrations took place in Jakarta, Yogyakarta and Bandung in West Java on Tuesday, as students and civil society groups voiced concerns over economic pressures, environmental damage and civil liberties. In Jakarta, hundreds of university students gathered around the Tugu Tani monument, demanding action on rising living costs and the government's handling of forest and peatland fires. The fires have generated toxic haze, disrupted flights, forced school closures and raised public health concerns. Protesters called on the government to declare the prolonged forest fires a national disaster, prosecute companies responsible for environmental damage, tackle corruption and make education and healthcare more affordable. They also demanded stronger protection for freedom of expression. According to RT, protesters in Indonesia also set a police truck on fire amid the unrest. Indonesia has struggled to contain forest fires in Sumatra, Kalimantan and Papua amid an unusually severe El Niño-driven dry season. The resulting haze has spread to neighbouring Singapore and Malaysia, prompting concerns over regional air quality and public health, The Jakarta Post reported. Amid the protests, Presidential Chief of Staff General Police Listyo Sigit Prabowo said President Prabowo Subianto chaired a limited meeting at Merdeka Palace in Jakarta on Monday to discuss accelerating efforts to tackle forest and land fires. In a post on X, Listyo said the President had instructed authorities to strengthen aerial operations and improve coordination among the Indonesian National Armed Forces, National Police, National Disaster Management Agency, local governments and communities. The President also called for investigations into 98 corporate cases suspected of being linked to forest and land fires to be expedited, Listyo said, adding that the Presidential Chief of Staff's office would oversee the government's response and ensure law enforcement proceedings were based on evidence and conducted in accordance with applicable regulations. Separately, Greenpeace Indonesia activists climbed the Welcome Monument at Jakarta's Hotel Indonesia traffic circle on Tuesday and unfurled large banners protesting what they described as the government's failure to address persistent wildfires, The Jakarta Post reported. (ANI)
